papers.title: On optimal Wannier decay in dimension three
papers.abstract: For a Chern nontrivial Bloch bundle over the three torus, we construct an orthonormal Wannier basis with the optimal pointwise decay $\mathcal{O}(|x|^{-5/2})$. All but one of the generators decay exponentially. This resolves the question left open in arXiv:2505.01999.

papers.title: A note on the failure of Payne's inequality on manifolds with boundary
papers.abstract: We show that Payne's conjecture on the comparison between Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues and buckling eigenvalues does not hold on flat and hyperbolic cylindrical surfaces and on (round) hemispheres.

papers.title: New graph invariants based on $p$-Laplacian eigenvalues
papers.abstract: We present monotonicity inequalities for certain functions involving eigenvalues of $p$-Laplacians on signed graphs with respect to $p$. Inspired by such monotonicity, we propose new spectrum-based graph invariants, called (variational) cut-off adjacency eigenvalues, that are relevant to certain eigenvector-dependent nonlinear eigenvalue problem. Using these invariants, we obtain new lower bounds for the $p$-Laplacian variational eigenvalues, essentially giving the state-of-the-art spectral asymptotics for these eigenvalues. Moreover, based on such invariants, we establish two inertia bounds regarding the cardinalities of a maximum independent set and a minimum edge cover, respectively. The first inertia bound enhances the classical Cvetkovi\'c bound, and the second one implies that the $k$-th $p$-Laplacian variational eigenvalue is of the order $2^p$ as $p$ tends to infinity whenever $k$ is larger than the cardinality of a minimum edge cover of the underlying graph. We further discover an interesting connection between graph $p$-Laplacian eigenvalues and tensor eigenvalues and discuss applications of our invariants to spectral problems of tensors.

papers.title: Flexibility of eigenvalues for graph Laplacians arising from genus 3 surfaces
papers.abstract: It is known that the small eigenvalues of the Laplacian of a Riemann surface close to the boundary of the modular space can be well approximated by the eigenvalues of the discrete Laplacian on a certain graph coming from the pair of pants decomposition of the surface. In this paper, we provide a complete description of the sets of eigenvalues of the weighted graph Laplacian for all graphs on four vertices that correspond to a valid pair of pants decomposition of a surface of genus 3.

papers.title: A note on the A.C. spectrum of limit-periodic Jacobi matrices
papers.abstract: We show that limit-periodic Jacobi matrices in the weak exponential class $EC(\eta)$ have purely absolutely continuous spectral type when $\eta$ is sufficiently large, depending only on the $R$-boundedness constant. The proof first establishes homogeneity of the spectrum from the weak exponential approximation rate. A closure theorem for reflectionless Jacobi matrices then transfers reflectionlessness from the periodic approximants to the limit, and a theorem of Poltoratski and Remling rules out singular spectrum on a homogeneous set.

papers.title: New Qualitative and Quantitative Estimates for Neumann Eigenvalues toward P\'olya's Conjecture
papers.abstract: We introduce the Enhanced Neumann P\'olya inequality, which is stronger than P\'olya's conjecture, and verify it for many classes of domains, including strip-tiling domains, Euclidean balls, thin product domains, and certain higher-dimensional tiling domains. We develop a geometric removal approach for the Enhanced Neumann P\'olya inequality. In particular, our results provide new classes of domains satisfying the Neumann part of P\'olya's conjecture.

papers.title: Quantitative P\'olya inequalities for annular sectors
papers.abstract: We prove explicit positive corrections to the Dirichlet and Neumann P\'olya inequalities at every positive eigenvalue index of every annular sector. The coefficients depend only on the radii and are uniform in the aperture. Real-order angular integration preserves the exact area term, while directional rounding estimates and radial trials control all frequencies. Optimized bounds attain the sharp circular-arc coefficient for the continuous count. We identify the full sector perimeter asymptotic and a low-index obstruction to using its coefficient throughout the spectrum. The strict Neumann inequality also passes to products with bounded Lipschitz domains.

papers.title: Spectral Theory of an Exactly Solvable Quantum-Optical Oscillator
papers.abstract: We study a one-dimensional single-excitation model of a scalar photon field coupled to a continuum of two-level atoms with quadratic density. The resulting matrix Hamiltonian has an unbounded spatially varying coupling and is not semibounded. We prove that it is essentially self-adjoint and determine its spectrum explicitly. The continuous spectrum is the half-line $(-\infty,\Omega]$, where $\Omega$ is the atomic resonance frequency, while the spectrum above $\Omega$ consists of a strictly increasing sequence of simple eigenvalues. These eigenvalues are characterized by the interlaced zeros of the Airy function and its derivative and satisfy \begin{align*} \omega_n = \left(\frac{3\pi g n}{4}\right)^{1/2} + \frac{\Omega}{4} + O(n^{-1/2}). \end{align*} The analysis is based on a nonlinear spectral reduction that yields a confining massless relativistic oscillator above $\Omega$ and an inverted oscillator below $\Omega$.

papers.title: Sharp Neumann eigenvalue means on triangles
papers.abstract: We prove two conjectures of Laugesen and Siudeja: the equilateral triangle uniquely maximizes the harmonic mean of the first two positive Neumann eigenvalues at fixed perimeter and their geometric mean at fixed area. The proof uses the two equilateral eigenfunctions and four projected polynomial corrections. Triangle symmetry reduces the associated variational matrices to two-by-two operations and two scalar invariants. Angular comparison and horizontal trial functions then yield the global inequalities. The same argument gives explicit quadratic stability bounds in terms of normalized side-length asymmetry.
